page_section: p. 11, Society (Brahmin Apex and Land Inducements)
original_excerpt: The Brahmins occupy the apex of the pyramid representing the caste hierarchy... Rajputs, the original founders of Chamba State, felt that without the Brahmin priests it could not be possible for them to perform religious rites. They invited them from the low-lying areas and offered inducements in the form of giving lands. Most of them entered the State during the period of Meru-Varman who constructed a large number of temples.
neutral_summary: Brahmin dominance in Chitrari originated from historical royal land grants by Rajput rulers (Meru-Varman) to maintain temple worship and ritual legitimacy.
term_notes: Refers to historic Sasana/Agrahara land endowments establishing temple-centered settlements.
coder_notes: Explains Brahmin demographic predominance (77% of population) and landownership.

original_excerpt: The dominance of one caste group led to the subordinate castes practically depending upon them... Aryas and Halis live aloof. Halis are the traditional ploughmen who cultivate land for the Brahmins under customary arrangements, but have adopted the Arya Samaj name to improve status.
neutral_summary: Brahmin landed dominance created structural economic dependence among Halis who performed plowing labour and later mobilized through Arya Samaj reform.
term_notes: Hali derived from hal (plough); Arya Samaj provided anti-untouchability identity.
coder_notes: Illustrates traditional agrarian dependence transitioning into socio-religious mobilization.

page_section: p. 45, Economy (Rainy Season Gujjar Milk Trade)
original_excerpt: Milk, therefore, does not form part of their daily diet and is practically non-existent. Even for the purpose of tea, powder milk is to be used. But during the rainy season the Gujjars (a nomadic tribe dealing with milk and its products) come in the nearby areas and settle on the dhars and from there the milk can however, be purchased.
neutral_summary: Severe shortage of local milk in Chitrari forces settled villagers to depend upon visiting nomadic Gujjars who camp on high alpine ridges (dhars) during monsoon.
term_notes: Dhars are alpine grazing pastures; highlights commercial pastoral-agrarian symbiosis.
coder_notes: Primary evidence of seasonal inter-community trade linking sedentary Hindus and pastoral Muslims.

original_excerpt: Bensis—This is the smaller caste and is traditionally engaged in playing music and pipes at temples and festive occasions, receiving customary dues from the villagers.
neutral_summary: Hereditary community of temple musicians performing at religious ceremonies in exchange for traditional village dues.
term_notes: Bensi is customary musical performer caste attached to Shakti Devi temple.
coder_notes: Documents specialized ceremonial service group in temple village economy.
